issue: Author is matched with instr(author, ?), which is case-sensitive and not the LIKE ? ESCAPE '\' the spec requires on both columns, so author search is not case-insensitive (AC2/AC3).
evidence: q=fowler -> instr('Martin Fowler', 'fowler') = 0 and the title 'Refactoring' has no 'fowler', so Refactoring is not returned; AC2 expects it.

issue: '_' is not escaped before the LIKE pattern, so it acts as a single-character wildcard (AC8).
evidence: query.replace(/\\/g, ...).replace(/%/g, ...) has no '_' replacement -> q=_ builds pattern '%_%', which matches every non-empty title instead of returning [].

issue: Off-by-one in the length check: a trimmed query of exactly 100 characters is rejected (AC6).
evidence: `if (q.length >= MAX_QUERY_LENGTH)` with MAX_QUERY_LENGTH = 100 -> q='a'.repeat(100) returns 400; the spec says 100 -> 200 and only 101 -> 400. Should be `>`.

issue: A repeated or non-string q is coerced with String() instead of being rejected with 400 { error: 'Query must be a single string' }.
evidence: `String(req.query.q ?? '').trim()` -> ?q=a&q=b gives req.query.q = ['a','b'], which becomes 'a,b', is searched and returns 200; the spec requires 400.

issue: The tests cover only AC1, AC4, AC6 (101 only) and AC7, so AC10 is not met. There are no tests for author match (AC2), case variants (AC3), trim (AC5), the 100-char boundary (AC6), wildcards % and _ (AC8), route order (AC9) or the repeated-q 400. Each high finding above slips through because of one of these gaps.
evidence: The describe block has 4 tests: q=CLEAN, q=%20%20, q=' OR 1=1 --, and 101 'a's -> 400.
